content: SQLite has no native TTL or row expiry. Standard table shape is key/value/expires_at; reads enforce expiry by comparing expires_at (NULL means no expiry) against a bound current-time parameter, and a sweep deletes rows with expires_at IS NOT NULL AND expires_at <= ?. An index on expires_at, optionally partial with WHERE expires_at IS NOT NULL matching the sweep predicate, keeps lookup and sweep cheap. Lazy expiry on read issues a best-effort DELETE for a key found expired. Growth: deletes never shrink the file; freed pages join the freelist and are reused, so a bounded key space stabilizes near its high-water mark. auto_vacuum must be configured before the first table or write; FULL moves pages on every commit, INCREMENTAL only reclaims when PRAGMA incremental_vacuum is run. In WAL mode the last connection close checkpoints and removes -wal; journal_size_limit can bound WAL growth.
